uncited: Geometry and Surface Priors align the discrete 3D Gaussian representation with continuous geometric priors to enforce positional and normal consistency, enabling accurate mesh extraction and physically-based rendering [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md].

Unlike methods relying solely on photometric loss, this family integrates geometric supervision into training or post-processing to ensure the Gaussians conform to physical surfaces [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md].
All methods in this family align the discrete Gaussian representation with a continuous geometric prior [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md].
The core mechanism adds geometric loss terms to the standard photometric rendering loss $\mathcal{L}_{rgb}$ [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md].

These losses enforce two properties: positional consistency, where Gaussian centers $\mathbf{c}_i$ are encouraged to lie on the zero-level set of a distance function (SDF or UDF) or align with metric depth estimates [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md], and normal consistency, where the orientation of the Gaussians (derived from their covariance matrix or rotation quaternion) is aligned with the surface normal estimated from the geometric prior [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md].
where $\mathcal{L}_{geo}$ is the geometric consistency loss and $\mathcal{L}_{norm}$ is the normal consistency loss [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md].
The weights $\lambda_{geo}$ and $\lambda_{norm}$ are hyperparameters that balance photometric fidelity against geometric accuracy [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md].

The integration of geometric priors into 3D Gaussian Splatting emerged to address the "floating" artifact issue inherent in the original 3DGS formulation, where Gaussians represent volume rather than surface [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md].
More recently, diffusion-based priors (Joint 2D and 3D Priors) have been introduced to leverage large-scale generative models for geometric regularization [20090-joint-2d-and-3d-priors.md].
